Short answer: WordPress offers a broad open ecosystem, Webflow offers a hosted visual system, and custom code offers control over exactly what is built. The best choice is the one your business can own and maintain.

What this means for your business

The platform does not create quality by itself. Scope, implementation, hosting, updates, accessibility, content, integrations, handoff, and ongoing care decide whether the site stays useful.

What to watch

  • A platform recommendation made before requirements.
  • Plugins or apps added without an owner and update plan.
  • Custom code with no repository, documentation, or recovery path.
  • An editor the real staff cannot use.

Do this next

  1. List required pages, repeated content, actions, integrations, and editors.
  2. Name who owns updates, hosting, accounts, code, and support.
  3. Build one representative page or flow before committing.
  4. Price launch, care, migration, and exit together.

When Little Fight fits

We use the right stack for the business and hand over the source, accounts, data, and instructions that belong to it. Custom is an option, not a personality test.
